title: Diagnosing a database incident
brief: Start with a slow request, select its causal branch from evidence and choose a bounded intervention.
outcomes: Separate pool delay, lock waits and expensive execution
Intervene without triggering a second overload
entry: An application request, connection/transaction ownership and basic transaction boundaries; detailed plans, lock protocols and capacity budgets are branch preparation.

neighbours.RL91: Owns deeper lock reasoning before a lock intervention.
neighbours.RL102: Owns admission and capacity budgets after a queue/saturation diagnosis.
neighbours.RL87: Owns plan interpretation and repair after expensive execution is established.
neighbours.RL86: Owns access paths when the execution branch needs them.

heading.title: The request’s missing time
heading.brief: Begin from a slow class-booking request and locally distinguish pool waiting, blocked server work and execution time. Use correlated timing and scope evidence to select a branch before detailed plan or capacity reading; missing measurements call for observation, not a guessed repair.

heading.title: A chain of waits
heading.brief: Follow a request to a root blocker, queue/saturation symptom or costly execution. Give enough local meaning to choose RL91 for unfamiliar lock reasoning, RL102 for admission/capacity, RL86/RL87 for access/plan work or RL92 for retained versions; take the chosen preparation before judging its intervention.

nested_article.title: Operating and diagnosing PostgreSQL
nested_article.brief: Use PostgreSQL evidence to separate blocked work, excessive work and connection pressure.
outcomes: Trace a request through pool and server waits
Test a targeted operational intervention and its recovery cost
nested_article.entry: General incident triage and a PostgreSQL application connection; prepare native plans or vacuum only for the selected investigation.

heading.title: An intervention with a limit
heading.brief: Once the causal branch and its needed understanding are established, compare targeted cancellation, termination, admission reduction or query repair; account for rollback and business effects. A supported lock-only diagnosis can stop here and in follow-up without opening index, plan or capacity explanations.

heading.title: Recovery without a surge
heading.brief: Drain or reject queued work deliberately, observe error and latency recovery, preserve evidence and correct the protocol that created the incident.

nested_article.title: Connections, overload and capacity
nested_article.brief: Budget admitted work and recovery headroom around the resource that actually limits the service.
outcomes: Distinguish connections, active work and queued requests
Choose bounded overload behaviour and capacity evidence
nested_article.entry: Application pools and basic transaction boundaries; deeper query, lock and version mechanisms are preparation for the capacity branch that uses them.
